# Documentation rework

Handover for the `docs/rework` branch. Per `AGENTS.md`, planned work belongs in GitHub Issues; this file is the branch's active handover. The developer decided on 2026-11-26 to keep it under `plans/` while the work runs on this branch.

**Decision status**: On 2026-10-22 the developer accepted the audience split, the trims, the merges, a custom figure style without Mermaid and chart data generated by the documentation test suite. On 2026-11-26 the developer decided to continue on `origin/docs/user-guide-improvements` and to keep the page name "Execution nodes": an execution node is anything in the execution layer, and an executor is one. On 2026-11-26 the developer approved the mockups and the figure style, asked for an animated home hero, and decided that moved pages get their links updated instead of redirect stubs. The content changes so far were reviewed as reasonable.

**Implementation status.** Packages 0 through 6 are implemented on this branch. The staged changes include the five-section navigation, the published figures and example pages, and the documentation specs that validate their outputs and figure data.

**Branch**: `docs/rework`, created on 2026-11-26 from `origin/docs/user-guide-improvements` at `5b5a2b2b`, which is one commit on `main` at `15e788d7`. The first attempt started from `9c567b9e` on `operator-unification`; its uncommitted diff was ported by hand because main had rewritten the guide in the meantime.

Editing this plan does not authorize Git operations.

## 1. Problem

The user guide is written for three audiences at once. Pages start at user level and then drift into internals. The docs have almost no visuals: one hand-built CSS flow chart, now copied onto three pages (`guide/index`, `core-concepts`, `running-algorithms`), and one GIF. Several printed outputs are labeled "illustrative" and nothing checks them.

Findings by page, re-checked against this branch on 2026-11-26:

- `invariants-and-validation` (290 lines): the user part now leads ("Check whether an operator fits your search space", "Choose the right check"). Declaring invariants and how compositions answer for what they resolve are still author material.
- `observability-and-analysis` (237 lines, "Analysis"): aspects and pointcuts are gone. "Observations, clocks and sources of your own" is still author material.
- `operator-composition` (433 lines): the catalog is user material; "Authoring a composition", the stateful composition and the concurrent cache wrapper are author material.
- `algorithms`: choosing an algorithm and the construction forms are user material; how recommendations resolve is author material.
- `running-algorithms` ("Algorithm runs"): the pause and resume lifecycle is still dense prose that a state diagram can carry.
- Duplicates: Overview and Core concepts still share the model and the flow chart. The numeric optimization example repeated Getting started; it was replaced on 2026-11-26.
- Glossary: still opens with the status labels.
- Extending: still a group inside the Guide; `writing-algorithms`, `writing-meta-algorithms`, `writing-operators` and `writing-wrappers` link into `/contributing/architecture`.
- Experiments: fixed on 2026-11-26. The page printed illustrative outputs from a configuration that reached `0` in nearly every grid cell; it now runs four-dimensional Rastrigin, states the configuration and quotes real outputs that `ExperimentDocumentationSpecs` pins.

Settled since the first review: the contributing index lists Layering and Execution resolution, and the run lifecycle has moved from Analyzer architecture to Algorithm runs.

## 2. Accepted decisions

- **Scope.** The rework covers the whole site: guide, examples, extension material, reference and contributing pages.
- **Audience split.** The top navigation has five sections, one reader each: Guide (use HeuristicLib), Examples (complete tasks to copy), Extend (write your own parts), Reference (look things up) and Contributing (change HeuristicLib itself).
- **User level.** User pages keep only what a user needs. Execution internals move to Extend or Contributing.
- **Merges.** Overview and Core concepts become one Introduction. Duplicate explanations collapse into the page that owns the concept.
- **Errors.** Every factual error found along the way is fixed.
- **Figures.** One custom figure system, no Mermaid: hairline cards, the brand blue for the subject, one orange accent for the single thing to notice, grey for context, API names in monospace chips. Every chart has a legend or direct labels, a hover readout and a data table, in light and dark mode.
- **Chart data.** The documentation test suite runs the documented configurations and writes the chart data as JSON, following the `<<<` snippet imports this branch already uses.
- **Mockups first.** The figure style and the site map are approved as mockups before pages change.
- **Names.** "Execution nodes" keeps its name. Page names from `docs/user-guide-improvements` are adopted.
- **Compare algorithms.** On 2026-11-26 the developer accepted replacing the numeric optimization example with Compare algorithms; its "Change the configuration" section moves to Configurations.
- **Real outputs.** Pages quote real outputs, and the documentation spec that runs the code pins them. Accepted on 2026-11-26 for Experiments.

## 3. Site map

**Guide**

- Start: Introduction (merged), Getting started.
- Model a problem: Problems, Search spaces, Objectives and candidates.
- Configure a search: Algorithms (trimmed), Operators, Configurations, Composing operators (split), Validation and invariants (split).
- Run and analyze: Algorithm runs (trimmed), Analysis (split), Search states, Randomness, Experiments.
- Domains: Data and machine learning, Symbolic expressions, Symbolic regression.
- Interop: Python.

**Examples**

- Solve a problem: Compare algorithms (new), Traveling salesperson, Symbolic regression, Custom problems, Multiobjective optimization.
- From Python: Symbolic regression from Python.

**Extend**

- Foundations: How execution works (new).
- Operators: Write an operator (merged), Write a composition (split), Define an operation (moved), Declare invariants (split).
- Algorithms: Write an algorithm, Write a meta-algorithm.
- Wrappers and analysis: Write wrappers, Observations and clocks of your own (split from Analysis).

**Reference**

- Terms: Glossary (moved).
- Catalogs: Algorithms and defaults (new), Operators by encoding (new), Analyzers and traces (new).

**Contributing**

- Start: Start contributing (new), Writing documentation (new).
- Principles: Design goals, Requirements, Developer guidelines.
- Architecture: Architecture overview (new), Layering, Execution nodes, Execution resolution (trimmed), Operator implementation (trimmed), Analyzer architecture (trimmed).

Removed since the first site map: Aspects and pointcuts, Write custom advice and Make an operation observable, because main replaced custom advice with configuration wrappers.

## 4. Figures

Figures included in the approved pilot and initial rollout

- Home: a GA population converging on two-dimensional Rastrigin, three generations.
- Introduction: problem, algorithm and random source into a run, with the `RunStreaming` and `RunToCompletionAsync` exits.
- Algorithms and Getting started: one GA generation with its configuration slots and the two mutation rates.
- Getting started: best, median and worst objective per generation, log scale.
- Traveling salesperson: the best tour at four generations; distance above the optimum, log scale.
- Multiobjective: initial population and final front with the chosen design; `h/r` along the front.
- Experiments: median heatmap over population size and mutation rate; per-trial dot plot.
- Algorithm runs: `AlgorithmRun` state diagram from `Ready`.
- Write wrappers: where one `Substitute` call places `[observe, time, count]` around an evaluator.
- Layering: layer stack with the dependency direction.

Figures added in the follow-up pass

- Search spaces: a small picture of each encoding.
- Multiobjective: a picture explaining dominance; the hypervolume curve the page now prints.
- Randomness: the fork tree from root to trials, iterations and operators.
- Analysis: a decision flow in place of the "Choose the right tool" table.
- Composing operators: a small tree per composition; per-item versus per-call choice; a limit inside versus outside a cache.
- Validation and invariants: what an operator keeps versus what the space states.
- Symbolic regression: a rendered expression tree and the data plotted against the fitted model.
- Custom problems: capacity usage bars that show the assembly bottleneck.
- How execution works: configuration versus executor.

## 5. Work packages

0. **Factual fixes.** Ported; see § 6.
1. **Mockups** of the site map and the figure style. Approved.
2. **Figure system.** VitePress theme components for figure cards, diagrams and charts, with a data table toggle and light and dark tokens.
3. **Data pipeline.** Specs in the documentation test suite verify or regenerate the chart JSON and check the outputs the pages quote. The docs build reads the committed JSON.
4. **Restructure.** Navigation, moves, merges, splits and updated links.
5. **New pages.** How execution works, the Reference catalogs, Start contributing, Writing documentation, Architecture overview.
6. **Figures on pages**, then a full link and anchor check.

A genetic algorithm and a hill climber run on ten-dimensional Sphere and Rastrigin with a budget of 20,000 evaluated candidates and twenty seeds. Pilot of packages 2 and 3:

- Components in `docs/.vitepress/theme/figures`: `HlFigure.vue` (card, caption, data table toggle), `LineChart.vue` (log or linear y, legend, end labels, one note, hover readout), `scales.ts` and `figures.css`, which maps the figure tokens onto VitePress tokens and `.dark`. Both components are registered globally in `theme/index.ts`.
- Each figure has a settings file in `docs/.vitepress/figures`, such as `getting-started-convergence.ts`, which imports its data and states how to draw it. A page imports it in `<script setup>` and writes `<LineChart v-bind="convergence">` with the caption as content; a multi-line component tag would be flattened by Prettier.
- Data files live in `docs/.vitepress/figure-data`, excluded from Prettier. `FigureData.Verify` in `HeuristicLib.Tests.Docs` compares a spec's data with the committed file and fails when it differs; with `HEURISTICLIB_UPDATE_FIGURE_DATA=1` it writes the file instead. Values are rounded to six significant digits. The docs CI job runs no .NET, so the files are committed.
- `GettingStartedDocumentationSpecs.TheProgressFigureShowsEveryGenerationOfTheStreamedRun` writes the convergence data and pins the five printed stream lines.
- The home hero animation is planned with the same components: plain SVG or canvas driven by Vue, no library, with the static panels as the reduced-motion fallback.
